topic: Reverse-Engineering Claude Web's Hidden Antspace MicroVM

key_points: Original AprilNEA reverse-engineering writeup (2026-03-18): casual strace -p 1 revealed Claude Code Web runs on Firecracker microVMs
Layer 1: Firecracker MicroVM identified via ACPI OEM ID 'FIRECK' / creator ID 'FCAT' — same tech as AWS Lambda and Fargate
Layer 2: Unstripped 27MB Go binary 'environment-runner' with full debug symbols leaked internal package structure
Layer 3: 'Antspace' — undocumented Anthropic PaaS with mature deployment protocol (streaming NDJSON status)
Documented snapstart snapshot/restore pattern and the process_api PID 1 init/supervisor wire protocol
Full GitHub repo with decompiled sources: 446K-line C pseudocode of process_api (3599 functions)
process_api = Rust/tokio PID 1 binary: firecracker_init, control_server, cgroup, oom_killer, proc_handle, state, adopter
Complete WebSocket wire protocol: JWT auth -> ProcessConnection -> CreateProcess, binary stdin/stdout/stderr framing, SendSignal, Resize, Detach, KeepAlive
HTTP control API port 2025: /status, /fs_sync, /shutdown, /auth_public_key, /mount_root (snapstart), /container_name
Block devices: vda=ext4 rw rootfs, vdb=squashfs claude-code, vdc=squashfs env-runner
Layer-by-layer breakdown: Firecracker microVM → environment-runner Go binary → Antspace client → Baku web app builder → BYOC
Baku = internal codename for claude.ai web app builder: Vite+React+TS template, supervisord dev server, auto-provisions Supabase via 6 MCP tools
Commercial insight: Baku's DEFAULT deploy target is Antspace, not Vercel; Vercel only an alternative
BYOC (envtype/byoc package) lets enterprises run environment-runner on their own infrastructure while Anthropic API orchestrates
No security disclosure: no exploits, no privilege escalation — pure introspection of an unstripped binary
HN discussion (109 points, 23 comments): title corrected — it's for Claude Code, not Claude web broadly
simonw asks key question: how do you actually USE the deployment platform; does the deployment persist after session ends
Community interest centers on whether Antspace is a real product launch vs internal infra
Repeated posting (third time) signals sustained community attention and high search demand
Contrast layer: Claude Code's LOCAL sandbox (Bash sandbox) is different from the Antspace cloud microVM
macOS uses Apple's Seatbelt, Linux/WSL2 uses Bubblewrap + network proxy; native Windows unsupported
Local sandbox allows/deny filesystem rules and network-domain approval; can fall back to unsandboxed execution
Distinguishes 'containing the tool' (local sandbox) vs full-hardware-isolation (microVM) — a useful framing hook
Relevant for readers wanting to replicate Anthropic's isolation approach in their own agents

stats.fact: Claude Code Web session ran on Firecracker microVM: 4 vCPUs (Intel Xeon Cascade Lake @ 2.80GHz), 16GB RAM, 252GB disk, Linux kernel 6.18.5
Firecracker is identified via ACPI tables signed with OEM ID 'FIRECK' and creator ID 'FCAT'; it is the same MicroVM technology powering AWS Lambda and Fargate
The environment-runner binary is a 27MB unstripped Go binary with full debug symbols; built from github.com/anthropics/anthropic/api-go/environment-manager/
process_api is a 3.1MB Rust/tokio binary, PID 1 init/supervisor, decompiled to 3599 functions / 446K lines of C pseudocode via Ghidra
Sessions resume from frozen VM snapshots (Snapstart pattern); dmesg showed a 48.5-hour gap between template boot and session restore; ext4 rootfs mount count=11 (reused across 11 sessions)
Antspace has ZERO public documentation — a search of Anthropic's site, GitHub, blog, docs, LinkedIn, job postings, conference talks and patents returned nothing; version string prefixed 'staging-'

Antspace deployment protocol is mature: 3 phases (create deployment, upload build artifact, stream deployment status) using application/x-ndjson streaming; file upload = single tar.gz archive vs Vercel's SHA-dedup per-file
Baku (claude.ai web app builder) auto-provisions a Supabase backend via six built-in MCP tools and defaults to deploying on Antspace rather than Vercel

Security hardening includes init_on_free=1 (zero freed pages), dropping CAP_SYS_RESOURCE after init, CRNG reseed on snapshot restore, and --block-local-connections; block devices are hot-swapped at restore

angles: An AI-native PaaS play: Antspace + Baku + Supabase forms a fully vertical pipeline (intent → Claude → Baku → Supabase → Antspace → live app) where the user never leaves Anthropic's ecosystem — reframes Anthropic as platform competitor, not just model provider
Build hygiene lesson: shipping an unstripped Go binary with full debug symbols to production exposed Anthropic's entire internal architecture — a reusable warning for anyone shipping agent runtimes

Reusable RE methodology: the exact Linux-tooling cookbook (dmesg|grep FIRECK, cat /proc/1/cmdline, go version -m, objdump -t, symbol-table grep) that anyone can apply to any sandboxed agent environment
Security vs marketing framing: this is NOT a security exploit — no privileges escalation, just standard introspection; separates hype from substance for a technical audience
Cold-start engineering: Snapstart deferred-mount pattern achieves near-instant session restore (<30ms) vs traditional VM boot — deep-dive on why snapshot/restore beats cold boot
Enterprise control point: BYOC (envtype/byoc) lets enterprises run environment-runner on their own infra while Anthropic orchestrates — relevant for regulated/hybrid-cloud buyers
What it means for builders: Firecracker-based agent sandboxes are becoming the default infra layer for coding-agent platforms — practical guidance for replicating isolation in your own stack
